items.title: Edwin "Squirrel" Ashcraft Interview, 1961-08-16
items.q: I'm not too sure they did. They were inclined to separate the white and Negro musicians... heard the Oliver Band... heard Louie

ctx.x: Down here on Madison Street, just about south of us, Madison and Halsted, or Madison and Ashland, in that neighborhood. Maybe Tommy Thomas' or some of the joints that were then popular in that area. That was a hot area.

Yeah. That's why I don't, I think that it wasn't until after Bud, Tesh, and the others had heard Louie, or rather heard the Oliver Band, out in the south side, that they really connected the two up. And I'm not too sure they did. They were inclined to separate the white and Negro musicians, partly because the economics of Chicago at that point had the Negro musician either playing on the south side or playing as an entertaining type of band. They used to think of moments as a clown band. And it would be only the…
There seems to be the possibility of some direct imitation. Would you think that Tesh might have imitated, might have studied records of Johnny Dodds?
